newsitem.title: USA: House votes to end Food Stamps to prisoners.
newsitem.headline: House votes to end Food Stamps to prisoners.

text.p: The House Tuesday ordered states to ensure that prison inmates stayed off the federal food Stamp rolls, a move expected to save millions of dollars.

By a vote of 409-0 the House passed legislation giving states one year to develop new safeguards to prevent county, state and federal inmates from being counted as household members for purposes of determining Food Stamp eligibility.

The bill came in response to a recent General Accounting Office review of Texas, New York, Florida and part of California that found 12,138 inmates were counted as family members, resulting in $3.5 million in Food Stamp overpayments.

Virginia Republican Rep. Bob Goodlatte, author of the measure, said it was unfair for a household to receive higher Food Stamp benefits than it deserved by "illegally counting an incarcerated member who is, after all, receiving three squares a day in the slammer."
The legislation must now be considered by the Senate. Inmates are already ineligible for Food Stamp aid, but states have been failing to make proper verification.
States that failed to comply with the legislation could lose part of their federally supplied funds for administering the Food Stamp program or face other actions.
